s: The slope of a distance-time graph shows .............. .
x: The slope of a distance-time graph is distance/time, which is speed.

s: The tendency of undisturbed objects to stay at rest or to keep moving with the same velocity is called
x: Inertia is the tendency of a body to stay at rest or in uniform motion (Newton's first law).

s: Which of the following quantity is a measure of inertia?
x: Mass measures inertia; weight depends on gravity.

s: The rate of change of momentum of a body is equal to the resultant
x: By Newton's second law, force = rate of change of momentum.

s: The Second Law of Motion states that
o: Every object will move in a uniform motion when a net force is applied.
The rate of change of momentum of an object is proportional to the net force applied on the object in the direction of net force.
Every object will remain at rest or in a state of uniform motion unless compelled to change its state by the action of a net force.
The rate of change of speed of a body will change with the net force applied.
x: Newton's second law says the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the net applied force, in the direction of the force. Option 3 is the first law.

s:
Statement I: When a gun is fired, it pushes back with much less velocity than the velocity of the bullet.
Statement II: Velocity of the recoiling gun is less because the gun is much heavier than the bullet.
Codes
o: Both the statements are individually true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I
Both the statements are individually true but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I
Statement I is true, but statement II is false
Statement I is false, but statement II is true
x: By conservation of momentum, the gun and bullet get equal and opposite momenta. The gun is much heavier, so its recoil velocity is smaller. Statement II therefore explains Statement I.

s: Which of the following physical quantity measures the rate of work done?
x: Power is the rate of doing work (work/time).

s: For a missile launched with a velocity less than the earth’s escape velocity, the total energy is
x: A body with speed below escape velocity is gravitationally bound, so its total energy (KE + PE) is negative.

s: The spring balance works on the principle of …… .
x: A spring balance works on Hooke's law: extension is proportional to the applied force.

s: 1 pascal equal 1 ……… .
x: Pascal is the unit of pressure, defined as force per area, so 1 Pa = 1 N m⁻².

s: According to ………, pressure is equal to the force divided by the area on which it acts.
x: The notes do not define pressure as force per area. By the question's convention this is attributed to Pascal's law, as in the key.

s: The pressure of a fluid varies with depth h as p = p0 + ρgh, where ρ is the fluid density. This expression is associated with
x: Pressure varying with depth as p = p0 + ρgh is the hydrostatic pressure relation, attributed to Pascal's law in the key.

s: Which of the following physicists explained the existence of Buoyant force?
x: Archimedes' principle explains buoyancy, so Archimedes explained the buoyant force.

s: Which law/principle states that when a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences an upward force that is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it?
x: The upward force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced is Archimedes' principle (buoyancy).

s: Purity of a metal can be determined with the help of
x: Archimedes' principle relates to buoyancy and the density of the body, and density helps check a metal's purity.

s: Decibel is the unit of
x: The decibel is the unit of sound level (intensity), as the notes list it among units.

s: Which one of the following frequency range is sensitive to human ears?
x: The audible range for humans is 20 Hz to 20 kHz, i.e. 20-20000 Hz.

s: The frequency of ultrasonic waves is
x: Ultrasound is sound above 20 kHz, the upper limit of human hearing.

s: What is called the sound wave above than frequencies of 30,000 Hz?
x: Sound above 20 kHz is ultrasound, so a wave above 30,000 Hz is ultrasound; infrasound is below 20 Hz.

s: In which of the following mirror size of image formed is always equal to the size of object?
x: A plane mirror always forms an image the same size as the object, whereas convex and concave mirrors change the size depending on object position.

s: Which one of the following is not true about the image formed by a plane mirror?
o: It is of the same size as the subject.
It is formed as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.
x: A plane mirror forms a virtual image, not a real one, so the statement that it is real is false; the other statements are true.

s: Which one of the following statement is correct for a plane mirror?
o: The size of the image of an object placed in front of the mirror is slightly less than that of the object.
The image is virtual, erect and laterally inverted.
x: A plane mirror gives a virtual, erect, laterally inverted image of the same size; its focal length is infinite, so the other options are wrong.

s: A curved mirror where the reflecting surface is curved inwards is called a
x: A concave mirror has its reflecting surface curved inwards (like the inside of a sphere); a convex mirror bulges outwards.

s: In which mirror, image formed is virtual, correct and point sized?
x: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image (point-sized for a very distant object); plane and concave mirrors do not do this for all positions.

s: If you look into a mirror and find that the image your reflexion is smaller than you, then the type of the mirror is
x: A convex mirror gives a diminished image (magnification less than 1), so the image looks smaller.

s: What is the Centre of Curvature of a spherical mirror?
o: It is a point from which the rays of light appear to be coming from on the principal axis a convex mirror.
It is the centre of a hollow sphere of which the spherical mirror is a part.
It is the midpoint of spherical mirror.
It is the point of the principal axis through which rays of light parallel to the principal axis pass after reflection.
x: The centre of curvature is the centre of the hollow sphere of which the mirror is a part.

s: Name the type of mirror used in the headlight of vehicles.
x: A vehicle headlight uses a concave mirror; a convex mirror is used as the rear-view mirror.

s: The mirror used by a dentist to examine the teeth of patients is
x: A dentist uses a concave mirror because with the object within the focus it gives an erect, magnified virtual image of the teeth.

s: Convex mirrors are used as a rear view mirror in motion cycles because
o: it forms smaller image as compared with object.
x: A convex mirror forms a virtual, erect, diminished image (magnification less than 1) and gives a wider field of view, so all the reasons given are true.

s: If objects appear enlarged and inverted in a rear view mirror, then which type of mirror is used?
x: A concave mirror can give an enlarged image and an inverted real image; a convex mirror always gives a diminished erect image, and a plane mirror gives a same-size image.

s: Concave mirror is used in headlights of vehicles, because it
o: focuses light from the bulb onto nearby vehicles.
fits well into the shape of the headlight.
x: The bulb sits at the focus of the concave mirror, so reflected light goes out as a parallel beam.

s: The outside rear view mirror of modern automobiles is marked with warning ‘objects in mirror are closer than they appear’. Such mirrors are
o: concave mirrors with very large focal lengths.
concave mirrors with very small focal lengths.
x: The rear-view mirror is convex, and its magnification below 1 makes objects look smaller and farther than they are.

s: In a concave mirror if object is placed at centre of curvature then image will be ……… .
x: When an object is at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror, the image forms at the centre of curvature, real, inverted and the same size.

s: What will be the size of image formed by a concave mirror when an object placed between pole and focus?
x: For an object between the pole and focus of a concave mirror, the image is virtual, erect and enlarged.

s: Find the position of the image formed by a concave mirror when the object is placed between P and F?
x: For an object between P and F of a concave mirror, the reflected rays diverge, so the virtual image forms behind the mirror.

s: In case of a concave mirror, if an object is kept between principal focus F and pole P of the mirror, then which one of the following statements about the image is not correct?
o: The image will be enlarged or magnified.
The image will be formed at infinity.
x: For an object between F and P of a concave mirror, the image is virtual, erect and magnified, and it is formed behind the mirror. It is not formed at infinity (that happens when the object is at F), so option 3 is not correct.

s: An object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror of focal length 16 cm. If the object is shifted by 8 cm towards the focus, then the nature of the image would be
x: The centre of curvature is at 32 cm (R = 2f). Moving the object 8 cm toward the focus puts it at 24 cm, which is between F (16 cm) and C (32 cm). The image is then real, inverted and magnified, beyond C.

s: In a magnifying glass ……… lens is used.
x: A magnifying glass is a convex lens. An object within its focal length gives a virtual, erect, magnified image.

s: When a convex lens produces a real image of an object, the minimum distance between the object and image is equal to
o: the focal length of the convex lens.
twice the focal length of the convex lens.
four times the focal length of the convex lens.
one-half of the focal length of the convex lens.
x: For a real image from a convex lens, the object-image distance is u + v. Its minimum is 4f, reached when the object is at 2f and the image is at 2f.

s:
A lens has a power of +2.0 Dioptre.
Which one of the following statements about the lens is true?
o: The lens is concave and has a focal length of 0.5 m.
The lens is convex and has a focal length of 2.0 m.
The lens is convex and has a focal length of 0.5 m.
The lens is concave and has a focal length of 2.0 m.
x: Power P = 1/f, so f = 1/2 = 0.5 m. A positive power means a convex (converging) lens, so option 3 is correct.

s: The light energy escaping from the sun can be spread by
o: a combination of a convex lens and a concave lens.
x: Rain drops spread sunlight into its colours by refraction and dispersion, as in a rainbow. A plane mirror or lens alone does not do this.

s: In long-sightedness, images are formed
x: In long-sightedness (hypermetropia) the eyeball is short or the lens is too weak, so the image of a near object forms behind the retina. A convex lens corrects it.

s: The lens-type commonly used for correcting presbyopia is ………
x: Presbyopia is age-related loss of near vision, and in many cases distance vision also needs correction. Bifocal lenses, which combine concave and convex parts, are commonly used for it.

s: The SI unit of electric charge is
x: The notes give 1 C as the unit of charge (1 C = 6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons). The SI unit of electric charge is the coulomb.

s: ……… is the “work done in moving a unit charge between two points in an electric circuit.”
x: Potential difference is defined as the work done per unit charge in moving it between two points in a circuit. Current, power and resistance are defined differently.

s: The frequency of direct current ………
x: Direct current flows steadily in one direction and does not alternate. Its frequency is therefore zero, unlike AC (50 Hz in India).

s: Ohm’s law states the relation between ……… and ……… .
x: Ohm's law relates potential difference (V) and current (I) through a conductor: V = IR at constant temperature.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding Ohm’s law is not correct?
o: Ohm’s law is an assumption that current through a conductor is always directly proportional to the potential difference applied to it.
A conducting device obeys Ohm’s law when the resistance of a device is independent of magnitude and polarity of applied potential difference.
A conducting material obeys Ohm’s law when the resistance of material is independent of the magnitude and direction of applied electric field.
All homogeneous materials obey Ohm’s law irrespective of whether the field is within range or strong.
x: Ohm's law is not universal. Many materials and devices (semiconductors, diodes, strong fields) deviate from it, so the claim that all homogeneous materials obey it is wrong.

s: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
x: Resistance is measured in ohms. Volt is potential difference and ampere is current.

s: Two wires are made having same length l and area of cross-section A. Wire 1 is made of copper and wire 2 is made of aluminium. It is given that the electrical conductivity of copper is more than that of aluminium. In this context, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: The resistance of wire 1 will be higher than that of wire 2.
The resistance of wire 2 will be higher than that of wire 1.
The resistance of both the wires will be the same.
If same current is flown through both the wires, the power dissipated in both the wires will be the same.
x: Resistivity is the inverse of conductivity, and R = ρl/A. With the same l and A, aluminium has lower conductivity, so it has higher resistivity and higher resistance than copper.

s: A wire bound standard resistor uses manganin or constantan. It is because
o: these alloys are cheap and easily available.
they have resistivity which almost remains unchanged with temperature.
x: Manganin and constantan have resistivity that is almost unchanged with temperature. This is why they are used in standard resistors.

s: Superconductors are substances which
o: offer high resistance to the flow of current.
offer no resistance to the flow of current.
x: Superconductors offer zero resistance to current below a critical temperature. Option 3 states this property.

s: When two resistors are connected in parallel, have ……… .
o: Both same current and different potential difference
x: Resistors in parallel are connected across the same two points. They therefore have the same potential difference, while the current divides.

s: The metal cap of an electric cell is generally the ……… terminal of the electrical cell.
x: The metal cap of a dry cell is its positive terminal, and the zinc case is the negative terminal.

s: Which of the following instruments is used to measure electric current?
x: An ammeter, connected in series, measures electric current. A voltmeter measures potential difference. A galvanometer only detects small currents.

s: The instrument used for detecting the presence of electric current in a circuit is
x: A galvanometer detects small electric currents in a circuit; refractometer, viscometer and diffractometer measure refractive index, viscosity and diffraction, so they cannot detect current.

s: The property of electric current which is applicable in the fuse wire is
x: A fuse works on the heating effect of current: the low-melting wire heats up and melts when current is excessive, breaking the circuit.

s: When a bar magnet is cut into two equal halves, the pole strength of each piece
x: Cutting a magnet always produces two complete magnets, each with north and south poles, because poles cannot be isolated. Each piece keeps the same pole strength, though its magnetic moment is halved.

s: The latest discovered state of matter is
x: Bose-Einstein condensate is the 5th and most recently discovered state of matter, after solid, liquid, gas and plasma.

s: The temperature at which a solid melts to become a liquid at the atmospheric pressure is called its melting point. The melting point of a solid is an indication of
o: strength of the intermolecular forces of attraction.
strength of the intermolecular forces of repulsion.
x: Melting requires overcoming the attractive forces holding particles together, so a higher melting point means stronger intermolecular forces of attraction.

s: Which chemical law proposes that ‘soft drinks and soda bottles are sealed under high pressure to increase the solubility of CO2?
x: Henry's law says gas solubility in a liquid increases with the pressure of the gas, so CO2 is dissolved in soft drinks under high pressure.

s: Why do two ice blocks join to form one block when pressed together ?
o: Melting point of ice is lowered with increase in pressure.
Melting point of ice increases with increase in pressure.
Melting point of ice remains unchanged with increase in pressure.
x: Pressure lowers the melting point of ice, so ice at the contact surfaces melts under pressure and refreezes when pressure is released, joining the blocks (regelation).

s: Which one of the following types of glass can cut off ultraviolet rays?
x: Crookes glass contains cerium oxide and absorbs ultraviolet rays, so it is used in protective spectacles. Soda, Pyrex and Jena glass transmit UV.

s: Distant objects can be seen with the help of
x: A telescope uses a convex lens or mirror to form images of distant objects; a microscope is for tiny nearby objects.

s: Two electrons in an orbital are differentiated by which of the following?
x: Two electrons in the same orbital have the same n, l and m values and differ only in spin quantum number (+1/2 and -1/2), per the Pauli exclusion principle.

s: Tyndall effect is related to the ……… of light.
x: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles, which makes the beam's path visible.

s: Which one of the following has highest frequency?
x: Cosmic rays have the shortest wavelength and so the highest frequency among the options, higher than X-rays, microwaves and radio waves.

s: Which is the most suitable unit for expressing nuclear radius?
x: Nuclear radii are of the order of 10^-15 m, which is one fermi (femtometre), so fermi is the suitable unit.

s: Which one of the following functions is not carried out by smooth endoplasmic reticulum?
x: Smooth ER synthesises lipids and steroid hormones and transports materials, but protein synthesis occurs on ribosomes of rough ER.

s: Darwin’s theory of natural selection is based on
x: Darwin's theory of natural selection includes overproduction, struggle for existence, variation and survival of the fittest, so all of these are correct.

s: The device used for measuring the wavelength of X-rays is
x: A Bragg spectrometer uses X-ray diffraction from crystal planes (nλ = 2d sinθ) to measure X-ray wavelength. A GM counter only detects radiation, a cyclotron accelerates particles, and a mass spectrometer measures mass.

s: Which one of the following does not convert electrical energy into light energy?
x: A candle produces light by burning, i.e. chemical energy. LED (electroluminescence), laser and TV convert electrical energy to light.

s: The speed of sound in air at 0°C is
x: The speed of sound in air at 0°C is about 331 m/s, written 331 ms⁻¹ with the correct unit.

s: Which law of physics states that the force between the two electric charges reduces to a quarter of its former value when the distance between them is doubled?
x: Coulomb's law says force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, so doubling the distance reduces the force to one quarter.

s: In step-down transformer, the AC output gives the
o: current more than the input current.
current less than the input current.
current equal to the input current.
voltage more than the input voltage.
x: A step-down transformer lowers voltage and, since power is nearly conserved, raises current, so output current is greater than input current. It works only on AC.

s: The SI unit of acceleration is
x: Acceleration is change in velocity (m/s) per unit time (s), so its SI unit is m/s², i.e. ms-2.

s: Which one of the following physical quantities does not affect the resistance of a cylindrical resistor?
o: The resistivity of the material used in the resistor.
The area of cross-section of the cylinder.
x: Resistance R = ρl/A depends on resistivity, length and cross-sectional area, not on the current passing through it.

s: Which one among the following components is used as an amplifying device?
x: A transistor can amplify signals; a transformer changes AC voltage, a diode rectifies and a capacitor stores charge.

s: Radioactive elements emit
x: Radioactive elements spontaneously emit alpha, beta and gamma radiations, not radio, infrared or ultraviolet waves.

s: Which of the following phenomena is involved in Kaleidoscope?
x: A kaleidoscope uses multiple reflections from inclined mirrors to form symmetric patterns.

s: According to law of reflection
o: Angle of incidence is greater than angle of reflection.
Angle of incidence is smaller than angle of reflection.
Angle of incidence is always equal to angle of reflection.
x: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence always equals the angle of reflection.

s: A person holding a pen in his left hand sees his reflection in the mirror holding the pen in his right hand. This is due to which of the following phenomena?
x: A plane mirror reverses left and right in the image, which is called lateral inversion.

s: When a ray of light travel from a denser medium to a rarer medium, it bends
o: towards the normal and slows down.
away from the normal and speeds up.
away from the normal and slows down.
towards the normal and speeds up.
x: Going from a denser to a rarer medium, light speeds up and bends away from the normal.

s: The absolute refractive index of air is
x: The absolute refractive index of air is about 1.0003.

s: An oscilloscope is an instrument which allows us to see waves produced by
x: An oscilloscope displays electrical signals; it is used to view sound waves (converted by a microphone) as waveforms.

s: If an object moves at a non-zero constant acceleration for a certain interval of time, then the distance it covers in that time
o: is independent of its initial velocity.
x: With constant acceleration, s = ut + ½at², so the distance covered depends on the initial velocity u.

s: ………are homogeneous mixtures of two or more components.
x: Solutions are homogeneous mixtures of two or more components; emulsions are colloids (heterogeneous), and enzymes are proteins.

s: Jellyfish are an example of which type of phylum ?
x: Jellyfish belong to phylum Cnidaria (coelenterates), which have stinging cells.

s: Wall lizard creep over the vertical wall and ceiling with the help of
o: adhesive pad found on their digits.
ventral side of body is adhesive.
x: Wall lizards (geckos) have adhesive pads on their digits that let them cling to vertical walls and ceilings.

s: The absolute zero is a temperature at which ………
o: molecular motion in a gas would cease
x: Absolute zero (0 K) is the temperature at which molecular motion would cease.

s: Why is it difficult to measure the coefficient of expansion of a liquid than solid?
o: Liquids tend to evaporate at all temperatures.
Liquids expand too much when heated.
Their containers also expand when heated.
x: The container also expands on heating, so the observed liquid expansion is only apparent, which makes measuring it difficult.

s: What is sublimation?
o: It is the process of conversion of a liquid into gas.
It is the process of conversion of a solid into liquid.
It is the process of conversion of a solid into vapour.
It is the process of conversion of a gas into liquid.
x: Sublimation is the direct change of a solid into vapour without passing through the liquid state.

s: Matter around us can exist in three different states, namely, solid, liquid and gas. The correct order of their compressibility is
x: Compressibility is lowest in solids and highest in gases, so Solid < Liquid < Gas.

s: An emulsion is a colloid of a
x: An emulsion is a colloid of one liquid dispersed in another liquid, e.g. milk (fat in water).

s:
Match the following. Process Changes

A. Evaporation
1. Liquid into gas

B. Sublimation
2. Solid into gas

C. Freezing
3. Solid into liquid

D. Melting
4. Liquid into solid
Codes A B C D A B C D
x: Evaporation is liquid to gas, sublimation solid to gas, freezing liquid to solid and melting solid to liquid, giving 1 2 4 3.

s: Which one of the following is not the result of surface tension?
o: Vapour formation above the liquid surface.
Spherical shape of mercury fallen on the floor.
x: Surface tension explains the meniscus shape, capillary rise and spherical mercury drops. Vapour formation is evaporation, which is a separate process and not a result of surface tension.

s: Among the following respiration is which type of process ?
x: Respiration oxidises glucose and releases energy as heat and ATP, so it is an exothermic process.

s: Which one of the following statement about the mass of a body is correct?
o: It changes from one place to another.
It does not depend on its temperature.
x: Mass measures inertia, which is a property of the body that does not change with place. Weight varies with location but mass does not.

s: The full form of SONAR is
x: SONAR stands for Sound Navigation And Ranging. It uses ultrasound echoes to detect and locate objects underwater.

s: Which one among the following transitions of electron of hydrogen atom emits radiation of the shortest wavelength?
x: Shortest wavelength means the largest energy gap. The n=2 to n=1 transition has the biggest gap among the options, so it emits the shortest wavelength.

s: Infrared, visible and ultraviolet radiations/ light have different properties. Which one of the following statements related to these radiations/light is not correct?
o: The wavelength of infrared is more than that of ultraviolet radiation.
The wavelength of ultraviolet is smaller than that of visible light.
The photon energy of visible light is more than that of infrared light.
The photon energy of ultraviolet is less than that of visible light.
x: Ultraviolet has a shorter wavelength than visible light, so its photon energy is higher. Statement 4 says it is lower, so it is the incorrect one.

s: In which region of electromagnetic spectrum does the Lyman series of hydrogen atom lie?
x: The Lyman series involves transitions to n=1, which emit high-energy photons in the ultraviolet region.

s: A photon of X-ray has energy of 1 keV. A photon of visible radiation has energy of 3 eV. In this context, which one of the following statement(s) is/are not correct?
o: The wavelength of X-ray photon is less than the wavelength of visible radiation photon.
Both the photons have different energies.
The speeds of both the photons in vacuum are different.
The frequency of X-ray photon is higher than the frequency of visible radiation photon.
x: All photons travel at the speed of light in vacuum, whatever their energy. So the claim that the two speeds differ is wrong.

s: What is weight?
o: Weight can be determined by only a spring balance.
The weight of a body is constant.
The force with which earth attracts towards its centre.
Weight of a body has a direction towards the centre of the earth. So it is a vector quantity.
x: Weight is the gravitational force with which the earth attracts a body towards its centre. It varies with location and can be measured in ways other than a spring balance.

s: The weight of a body at the centre of Earth is
o: half the weight at the surface
twice the weight at the surface
x: At the centre of the Earth, g is zero because the attractions cancel out, so the weight is zero.

s: The weight of an object on the moon is equal ……… of its weight on the earth.
x: The moon's gravity is about one sixth of the earth's, so weight on the moon is 1/6th of that on earth.

s: Barr body is absent in somatic cell of
x: A Barr body is an inactivated X chromosome. Turner syndrome (XO) has only one X, so it has no Barr body.

s: Which botanist is credited with creating one of the first widely used natural systems of plant classification ?
For which one of the following snakes the diet is mainly composed of other snakes ?
x: The king cobra is ophiophagous, feeding mainly on other snakes.

s: The snake who make their nest
x: The king cobra is the only snake that builds a nest for its eggs.

s: Which term is not associated with sound wave?
x: Candela is the unit of luminous intensity, so it is not related to sound. Hertz (frequency), decibel (loudness) and Mach (speed relative to sound) are all linked to sound.

s: The speed of a body that has mach number more than 1 is
x: Mach number is the ratio of a body's speed to the speed of sound. A value above 1 means the speed is supersonic.

s: Glass is soluble in
x: Hydrofluoric acid reacts with the silica in glass to form silicon tetrafluoride, so it dissolves glass. The other acids do not.

s: When a ray of light enters a glass slab, then
x: Frequency is set by the source and does not change on entering a new medium. Velocity and wavelength change instead.

s: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities have the same dimensions?
x: Work and energy both have the dimensions ML²T⁻². Power has different dimensions.

s: A molecule of a substance is similar to its atom for
x: A monoatomic molecule consists of a single atom, so the molecule is the same as the atom, as in noble gases.

s: Phosphorus is kept in water because
o: its ignition temperature is very high.
its ignition temperature is very low.
x: White phosphorus has a very low ignition temperature and catches fire in air, so it is stored under water.

s: Which of the following is NOT an unsaturated carbon compound?
x: Butane is a saturated alkane (only single bonds), whereas acetylene, pentene and benzene contain double or triple bonds and are unsaturated.

s: Methyl propane is an isomer of
x: Methylpropane (isobutane) has formula C4H10, the same as n-butane but with a branched chain, so they are structural isomers.

s: Which one of the following can charge an insulator?
In the equation of motion v = u + at , u represents ........... .
x: In v = u + at, u is the initial velocity and v is the final velocity.

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. There is no net moment on a body which is in equilibrium.

II. The momentum of a body is always conserved.

III. The kinetic energy of an object is always conserved.
Which of the statements (s) given above is/are correct?
x: Only statement I is correct: in equilibrium the net moment is zero. Momentum is conserved only when no external force acts, and kinetic energy is not conserved in inelastic collisions.

s: Sound is a form of …… that produces sensation of hearing.
x: Sound is a mechanical wave produced by vibrations and needs a medium, so it is mechanical energy, not an electromagnetic wave.

s: If the work done on the system or by the system is zero, then which one of the following statement for a gas kept at a certain temperature is correct?
o: Change in internal energy of the system is equal to flow of the heat in or out of the system.
Change in internal energy of the system is less than heat transferred.
Change in internal energy of the system is more than the heat flow.
x: By the first law, ΔU = Q - W. With W = 0, ΔU = Q, so the change in internal energy equals the heat flow.

s: Which phenomena shows the particle nature of light?
x: The photoelectric effect is explained by light as photons (particles). Diffraction, interference and polarisation show its wave nature.

s: Which of these is the energy conversion that happens in the process called photosynthesis?
x: In photosynthesis, plants convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.

s:
An electron and a proton starting from rest are accelerated through a potential difference of 1000 V.
Which one of the following statements in this regard is correct?
o: The kinetic energy of both the particles will be different.
The speed of the electron will be higher than that of the proton.
The speed of the proton will be higher than that of the electron.
The speed of the electron and the proton will be equal.
x: Both gain the same kinetic energy (qV), as the charges are equal in magnitude. Since KE = ½mv², the lighter electron gets the higher speed.

s: When a longitudinal wave moves through a certain medium; the quantity which is transmitted through the medium is
o: both material of the medium and energy
x: A wave transmits only energy through the medium; the particles just oscillate about their mean positions and the material is not carried along.

s: The average kinetic energy of the molecules of an ideal gas is directly proportional to
x: By kinetic theory, the average kinetic energy of ideal gas molecules is (3/2)kT, proportional to the absolute temperature.

s: Which one of the following groups of cellular organelles contains DNA?
x: Mitochondria, chloroplasts and the nucleus contain DNA. Golgi bodies, plasma membrane and ribosomes do not.

s: The light is composed of small particles, called ………
x: Light consists of packets of energy called photons, as in the quantum theory of light.

s: The elements of group in the Periodic table
x: Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons and hence similar chemical properties.

s: Which one of the following is not a periodic property i.e., does not show any trend on moving from one side to the other in the Periodic Table?
x: Radioactivity depends on nuclear stability, not on electron arrangement, so it shows no periodic trend. Atomic size, valency and electronegativity vary periodically.

s: Which of the following is the symbol of the metal that occurs in liquid form at ordinary temperature?
x: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal that is liquid at ordinary temperature. K, Ag and Pb are solids.

s: In a bi-polar junction transistor,
o: all the three regions (the emitter, the base and the collector) have equal concentrations of impurity.
the emitter has the least concentration of impurity.
the collector has the least concentration of impurity.
the base has the least concentration of impurity.
x: In a BJT the base is thin and lightly doped, the emitter is heavily doped and the collector is moderately doped.

s: Generally insects respire through
x: Insects breathe through tracheae that open to the outside by pores called spiracles.

s: Which of the following is widely used in making semiconductor chips?
x: Germanium is a metalloid semiconductor used in chips (with silicon); radium, sodium and sulphur are not used for this.

s: Which of the following elements has the lowest melting point?
x: Radon is a noble gas with a very low melting point (about -71 C), far lower than sodium, tin or radium.

s: The unit for measurement of energy is
x: The joule is the SI unit of energy; pascal measures pressure, and calorie and horsepower are not the SI energy unit (horsepower is a unit of power).

s: What is the name of the device used to convert alternating current into direct current?
x: A rectifier (using diodes) converts AC into DC; a transformer only changes AC voltage.

s: Which one of the following devices changes low voltage alternating current to high voltage alternating current and vice-versa?
x: A transformer works on AC and steps voltage up or down by mutual induction; generators and motors do not do this.

s: Which one of the following statements about proteins in mammalian cells is corrects?
o: Proteins in mammalian cells are synthesised in cell membrane.
Proteins in mammalian cells are not synthesised in cell membrane but directly absorbed from food.
Proteins in mammalian cells are synthesised in rough endoplasmic reticulum.
Proteins in mammalian cells are synthesised in Golgi apparatus.
x: Proteins are synthesised by ribosomes on the rough endoplasmic reticulum, not in the cell membrane or Golgi, and they are not absorbed directly from food.

s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

I. Metallic oxides are said to be basic oxides.

II. Non-metallic oxides are basic in nature.

III. All acids have similar chemical properties.
Codes
x: Metallic oxides are basic, while non-metallic oxides are acidic, so II is false; all acids share similar properties (H+ release), so I and III are correct.

s: Which of the following is a sweet smelling substance?
x: Esters have sweet, fruity smells; ammonia is pungent and alcohols are not typically sweet-smelling.

s: Ammonia (NH3) obtained from different sources always has same proportion of nitrogen and hydrogen. It proves the validity of law of
x: A compound always has the same elemental proportion by mass regardless of source, which is the law of constant (definite) proportions.

s: Which one of the following is used for writing on glass?
x: Hydrogen fluoride attacks and etches glass (silicon dioxide), so it is used to write on glass; graphite and others do not.

s: Liquid water is denser than ice due to
x: Hydrogen bonding makes ice an open lattice, so ice is less dense than liquid water.

s: Which compound, when dissolved in water, conducts electricity and forms a basic solution?
x: NaOH is a strong base that dissociates into ions, conducting electricity and giving a basic solution; HCl and CH3COOH are acids, and CH3OH does not ionise.

s: To weld metals together, high temperature required such a high temperature is obtained by burning
x: The oxyacetylene flame (acetylene burning in oxygen) gives the highest flame temperature (~3000 C), used for welding; nitrogen does not support burning.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct with regard to the material of electrical insulators?
o: Electrons do not flow easily through them.
They have more number of electrons than the protons on their surface.
x: Insulators have electrons, but they are tightly bound and do not flow easily; so option 2 is right.
